items.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material
items.summary: by Youwei Li, Haoyu Hu, Yujun Zhang, Gui Liu The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure.
items.author: Youwei Li, Haoyu Hu, Yujun Zhang et al.

items.title: Crafting of physical exhibits by undergraduate medical students: A mixed method study to assess the acquisition of higher-order cognitive skills and student perceptions
items.summary: by Rajesh Kathrotia, Swapnil Paralikar, Vinay Chitturi, Pradip Barde, Gaurav Sharma, Naresh Parmar, Vivek Kumar Sharma, Chinmay Shah Active learning engages students in some activity that induces them to reflect upon ideas and how they are using these ideas. It also involves the process of keeping students mentally, and often physically, active in their learning through activities that engage them in gathering information, thinking, and solving problems. This study was conducted to determine if creating physical exhibits fosters higher-order cognitive skills like problem solving and critical thinking (application and analysis, respectively). In this study, carried out in the Department of Physiology, 50 medical undergraduate students were divided into four batches of 12–13 students each.

items.title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience
items.summary: by Tarun RajBhandari, Sabin Pokharel, Yam Prakash Gurung, Rajan Bhusal, Bibek Banskota, Ashok Kumar Banskota Background Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. Materials and methods This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal’s only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method.
items.author: Tarun RajBhandari, Sabin Pokharel, Yam Prakash Gurung et al.

items.title: An explainable machine learning framework for cross-dataset chronic kidney disease risk prediction using hybrid data balancing
items.summary: by Jarin Tasnim Mumu, Ismail Hossain, Kazi Md. Tanvir Anzum Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health problem, and early detection is important for reducing complications and improving treatment. Machine learning has shown strong potential for CKD prediction, but many existing studies rely on single datasets, face severe class imbalance, and provide limited interpretability. These challenges reduce model reliability and make cross-dataset use in real clinical settings more difficult. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an interpretable and adaptable machine learning framework for CKD risk prediction across different datasets. The proposed hybrid explainable machine learning (HXAI-ML) framework used two public CKD datasets: the UCI CKD Risk Factor Prediction dataset as the source dataset and the Kaggle CKD dataset as the target dataset.
items.author: Jarin Tasnim Mumu, Ismail Hossain, Kazi Md. Tanvir Anzum

items.title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway
items.summary: by Fen Lou, Guochun Deng, Jiejuan Chen, Yijiang Jing, Ao Wang, Mazhong Zhang, Yongping Zhang, Bin Wang Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg).
items.author: Fen Lou, Guochun Deng, Jiejuan Chen et al.

items.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study
items.summary: by S. M. Riaduzzaman Niaz, Sumaia Jannat, Sheikh Abdullah Al Ashik, Md. Khairul Islam AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and non-toxic compounds. Target prediction integrated data from SwissTargetPrediction, BindingDB, and CTD, while DN-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, OMIM, and transcriptomic datasets (GSE154561, GSE154881, GSE217709, and GSE30528).
items.author: S. M. Riaduzzaman Niaz, Sumaia Jannat, Sheikh Abdullah Al Ashik et al.

items.title: Potential antimicrobial activity, antioxidant, and anti-wrinkle effects of Linum usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel
items.summary: by Ahmad M. Eid, Mohammed Hawash, Linda Issa, Areej Joma, Ansam Joma, Deema Tumeh Background Linum usitatissimum ( L. usitatissimum ) seeds have been reported to have several biological efficacies, such as antioxidant, anti-aging, sun protection, and antimicrobial actions. The present study aimed to develop L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel and evaluate its cosmeceutical and antimicrobial characteristics for use in topical applications. Method L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel formulations were prepared by optimizing the non-ionic surfactant (Tween® 20, Tween® 80, and Span® 80) using a self-nanoemulsifying technique, followed by the addition of Carbopol®. The droplet size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and rheological behavior of the emulgel formulations were measured.
items.author: Ahmad M. Eid, Mohammed Hawash, Linda Issa et al.

items.title: The impact of robot-assisted frameless brain biopsy on performance differences between junior and senior neurosurgeons
items.summary: by Carolin Albrecht, Tobias Mahler, Viktor M. Eisenkolb, Benedikt Wiestler, Claire Delbridge, Chiara Negwer, Bernhard Meyer, Arthur Wagner Objective Frameless stereotactic brain biopsy is a standardized and routinely performed neurosurgical procedure, frequently carried out by residents under supervision in academic centers. Robot-assisted (RA) guidance has been introduced to standardize workflow and reduce operator-dependent variability. This study investigates whether RA frameless biopsy reduces experience-related performance differences between residents and attending neurosurgeons compared with a manually operated frameless system (MFS). Methods We performed a retrospective, non-randomized cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing RA frameless stereotactic brain biopsy for intracranial lesions at a tertiary academic center between 2021 and 2025.
items.author: Carolin Albrecht, Tobias Mahler, Viktor M. Eisenkolb et al.

items.title: PIP5K isoforms and phosphoinositide molecular species in EGF-stimulated PIP 3 synthesis: A multi-method approach using enzyme genetic suppression and chemical inhibition in MCF10A cells
items.summary: by Iosif Alexandrou, Vikki Flemington, Martin E. Swarbrick, Sabina Cosulich, Phillip T. Hawkins, Len R. Stephens The membrane phospholipid PI(4,5)P 2 has structural functions and is a substrate for PLC and PI3K enzymes to generate Ins(1,4,5)P 3 , DAG and PI(3,4,5)P 3 signals. PIP5Ks, that 5-phosphorylate PI4P, are the major source of PI(4,5)P 2 in mammalian cells. Current thinking suggests distinct pools of PI(4,5)P 2 may be differentially generated by PIP5Kα, β and γ isoforms and involved in different physiological functions. Phosphoinositides are comprised of families of acyl-chain variants but are uniquely enriched in C38:4 species. There is evidence that PIP5Ks are selective for certain acyl chain species of PI(4)P.
items.author: Iosif Alexandrou, Vikki Flemington, Martin E. Swarbrick et al.

items.title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis
items.summary: by Gizem Altundal, Asuman Deniz Gümrü Celikel, Gülnaz Marsan Objective To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery. Methods In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher’s exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated.
items.author: Gizem Altundal, Asuman Deniz Gümrü Celikel, Gülnaz Marsan

items.title: Ecological traits predict extinction risk of the world’s traded carnivores
items.summary: by Erik Joaquín Torres-Romero, Maximilian L. Allen, Vincent Nijman, Moreno Di Marco, Christopher J. O’Bryan, Vincenzo Penteriani Wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss, yet how trade interacts with species’ ecological traits and extinction risk remains underexplored. Carnivores warrant special attention because they are disproportionately exploited and vulnerable to extinction compared to other taxa. We analyzed 171,637 international trade records spanning 50 years (1975–2024) for 129 carnivore species listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). We analyzed trade volumes across the globe and then used logistic regression to evaluate associations between ecological traits and extinction risk, as well as family-level differences in extinction risk.
items.author: Erik Joaquín Torres-Romero, Maximilian L. Allen, Vincent Nijman et al.

items.title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review
items.summary: by Tagese Yakob, Charuai Suwanbamrung, Cua Ngoc Le, Abebe Sorsa Badacho, Udomsak Saengow Background Hypertension affects more than 1.28 billion adults globally and remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, renal failure, and premature death. This burden is inconsistently distributed across Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where nearly three-quarters of adults live with hypertension. This gap is largely driven by poor adherence and low retention. This systematic review aims to assess the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on retention in care, medication adherence, and blood pressure among adult patients with hypertension in primary health care settings in LMICs.
items.author: Tagese Yakob, Charuai Suwanbamrung, Cua Ngoc Le et al.

items.title: Antiviral activity of Rumex crispus extract and its bioactive constituent emodin against human coronavirus OC43
items.summary: by Seungju Cho, Jang Hoon Kim, Siyun Lee, Chunghyeon Lee, Yong-Goo Kim, Eunji Cho, Jayhyun Park, Junsoo Park Coronaviruses are responsible for diseases ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe infections such as COVID-19. Despite the availability of vaccines and therapeutic agents, the emergence of new variants and drug-resistant strains highlights the need for additional antiviral strategies. In this study, Rumex crispus was investigated as a potential source of antiviral compounds. The ethanol (EtOH) extract of R. crispus roots was prepared and subsequently fractionated into n-hexane (n-hex), ethyl acetate (EA), and aqueous fractions. Among these, the n-hexane and EA fractions exhibited significant antiviral activity against human coronavirus OC43, as demonstrated by Western blot, qRT-PCR, and plaque assays.
items.author: Seungju Cho, Jang Hoon Kim, Siyun Lee et al.

items.title: Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are associated with improvements in household food security and dietary diversity among vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh: Findings from a pre-post comparison study
items.summary: by Munia Afroz, Sakib Rahman, Fahmida Akter, Md. Mokbul Hossain, Mahbub A.H.M. Latif, Owen White Nkhoma, Jecinter Akinyi Oketch, Raihana Bhuiyan, Kiross Tefera Abebe, Deepika Mehrish Sharma, Farhana Sharmin, Mohammad Zahidul Manir, Md. Lalan Miah, Anjuman Tahmina Ferdous, Rina Rani Paul, Malay Kanti Mridha Introduction Nutrition-sensitive interventions aim to improve or at least safeguard the underlying causes of malnutrition, especially among the most vulnerable populations. Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are effective strategies for improving household food security and dietary diversity in low-income settings. In 2021, the European Union (EU) and UNICEF, in collaboration with the Government of Bangladesh and partners, implemented nutrition-sensitive interventions combining two income-generating activities (IGAs): backyard poultry rearing and tailoring with asset transfers, direct cash support, and nutrition education for vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh.

items.title: Clinical supervision in public hospitals in Lesotho: Nurse managers’ support for registered nurses
items.summary: by Mpho Zakaria Shelile, Molekodi Jacob Matsipane, Seepaneng Salaminah Moloko-Phiri, Miriam Mmamphamo Moagi Background Clinical supervision is regarded as essential for nurse managers in diverse healthcare settings to enhance nurse satisfaction, competence, and retention, leading to improved nursing care quality. The study aimed to explore and describe nurse managers’ support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision at public hospitals in Lesotho. Methods The study employed an exploratory descriptive qualitative research design to explore and describe the support provided to registered nurses during clinical supervision. Data was gathered through eight in-depth individual face-to-face interviews with participants purposefully selected from the public hospitals in Lesotho.
items.author: Mpho Zakaria Shelile, Molekodi Jacob Matsipane, Seepaneng Salaminah Moloko-Phiri et al.

items.title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
items.summary: by Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li, Yan Zhou Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations.
items.author: Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li et al.

items.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
items.summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$.
items.author: Samit Ganguly, Surhud More, Goutam Manna et al.

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields.
items.author: Tai Hyun Yoon

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.
items.author: Wan-Peng Gao, Xiao-Liang He, Zheng-Qi Niu et al.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model.

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate.

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs). In the case of low-frequency resonators, the equivalent temperature of the mechanical mode is orders of magnitude lower than the thermodynamic temperature of the device, implying that accessible TTLS states are largely saturated. We demonstrate that the observed temperature and drive dependence of the losses fit well within the framework of an interacting TTLS bath, indicating the presence of a channel for energy transfer between the mechanical mode and thermally activated TTLSs.

items.title: Continuous variable payload transmitter for the SPOQC mission
items.summary: The continuous variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme enables two parties to share a secret key separated by a certain distance. Here we propose, design, build, test and show results of a CV payload transmitter, intended to demonstrate downlink based QKD from a CubeSat in low earth orbit. This is part of the SPOQC mission by Quantum Communications Hub, UK which was successfully launched on March 2026.

items.summary: “I see” IC 342, the Hidden Galaxy! Today’s image peers through the plane of the Milky Way, through all its gas, dust and stars, to unveil this spiral galaxy. IC 342 (or Caldwell 5) is one of the brightest members of the IC 342/Maffei group of galaxies. Located about 10 million light years away, this group is quite close to the Local Group that includes our Milky Way. Inaccurate accounting of the crowded and dusty Milky Way foreground has led to misunderstandings in IC 342’s history, including the theory that the galaxy was ejected from the Local Group. IC 342 has its own dust intermittently blocking the glow of hydrogen gas, indicating the presence of bright, young stars.
